title: Outreach vs Salesloft: which should you choose in 2026?
summary: An honest 2026 comparison of Outreach and Salesloft after the Clari merger, across cadence, forecasting, AI, stability, and pricing.
body_markdown:
Outreach and Salesloft are the two enterprise sales engagement incumbents, and they are more alike than different: mature cadence governance, deep CRM sync, and reporting built for large orgs. The 2026 decision hinges on two things. Salesloft closed a merger with Clari on December 3, 2025, adding forecasting but raising roadmap questions. Outreach stayed independent.


For years these were the default two-tool shortlist for any enterprise buying sales engagement. The core capability, running disciplined multichannel cadences that tell reps what to do next, is close to a tie. What separates them now is corporate direction: Salesloft's move into a combined cadence-plus-forecasting company, and Outreach's steadier, standalone path with its own AI agent. This comparison weighs both fairly.

## What is the difference between Outreach and Salesloft?


At the feature level, less than most buyers expect. Both run multichannel cadences across email, calls, and social outreach, both enforce process across large rep teams, and both sync deeply with the CRM and report on activity. If you put the two cadence builders side by side, an experienced ops leader would find them comparably capable.


The difference is strategic. Salesloft is now part of a combined company with Clari, so its story is cadence plus forecasting from a single vendor. Outreach is a focused, independent sales engagement platform that added its own AI agent rather than a forecasting suite. So the real question is not which sequencer is better, it is which corporate bet fits your roadmap and your appetite for change.


## Which has better cadence and workflow governance?


This is close to a tie, and that is the honest answer. Both were built for large, disciplined sales organizations and both offer deep sequence controls, team permissions, and step-level reporting. Neither has a governance gap the other exploits. Teams that have run both tend to describe the choice as a matter of taste and existing integrations rather than a capability gap.


Outreach edges slightly ahead on being a single-focus product: its entire roadmap goes into engagement. Salesloft's attention is now split across a broader cadence-and-forecasting platform. Whether that is a plus or a minus depends on whether you value forecasting integration or focused engagement investment. On raw cadence governance alone, treat them as even and let the tiebreakers decide.


## What did the Salesloft and Clari merger change?


The merger closed December 3, 2025, combining Salesloft's cadence with Clari's forecasting and revenue analytics under one roof. For a buyer who wants execution and forecasting from the same vendor, that is a genuine draw, and it is Salesloft's clearest differentiator against Outreach right now. For background, Vista Equity Partners recapitalized Salesloft in 2022 in a deal reported at around $2.3 billion.


The flip side is uncertainty. Any merger this size leaves new buyers unsure where the combined product is headed, which features get prioritized, and how integrations evolve. Those are fair questions to raise in a sales conversation. Separately, Salesloft's former sibling product Drift suffered a 2025 supply-chain breach reported by Google threat intelligence, and its retirement was announced in March 2026. Drift is a distinct product from Salesloft's core engagement platform, but the history is worth knowing when you evaluate the wider portfolio.


## Which is better for forecasting?


Salesloft, because of the Clari merger. If you want your cadence platform and your forecasting to come from the same company, with tighter integration between rep activity and revenue prediction, the combined Salesloft-Clari entity is built for exactly that. That is the strongest single reason to pick Salesloft over Outreach in 2026.


Outreach does not ship native forecasting in the same way. Teams using Outreach typically pair it with a separate forecasting tool. If forecasting is central to how you run the business and you would rather not stitch two vendors together, Salesloft's combined story wins this category outright.


## How do they compare on price?


Both are enterprise purchases sold through a sales process, not self-serve, and neither publishes pricing. Outreach's reported figures sit around $100 to $160 per user per month (an estimate, low confidence), often with implementation fees estimated at roughly $5,000 to $25,000. Salesloft's numbers come through negotiation; third-party estimates put it around $125 to $165 per user per month (low confidence), with its dialer typically an add-on billed separately.


Because both are quoted rather than listed, the real number depends on volume, term, and what modules you take. With Salesloft, factor in the forecasting side of the combined platform; with Outreach, factor in the separate forecasting tool you may need. Price is unlikely to be the deciding factor between these two; fit and stability are.


## A third option to know about


Both tools share one structural limit: whichever you pick, they tell a rep what to do next, and the rep still writes, sends, calls, and replies. Their AI features assist that person rather than replace the work. If what you actually want is the software to do more of the work rather than schedule it, an AI-driven platform is a third path.

## Choose Outreach if


-


You want a stable, independent enterprise sequencer without merger uncertainty.


-


Deep cadence governance and process control across many reps is your priority.


-


You already have or prefer a separate forecasting tool.


-


You want a focused engagement product whose full roadmap goes into that job.


-


The Omni agent inside a mature platform is the AI story you want.


## Choose Salesloft if


-


You want cadence and forecasting from one vendor, via the Clari merger.


-


Tight integration between rep activity and revenue prediction matters to your motion.


-


You are comfortable with post-merger roadmap questions in exchange for that combined platform.


-


Your enterprise process needs mature, disciplined cadence governance, which Salesloft matches.


-


You value the broader revenue-operations story the combined company tells.


## Frequently asked questions


### Are Outreach and Salesloft basically the same?


On core cadence capability, they are close. Both run disciplined multichannel sequences, enforce process across large teams, and sync deeply with the CRM. The meaningful differences are corporate: Salesloft merged with Clari on December 3, 2025 to add forecasting, while Outreach stayed independent and added its Omni agent in April 2026. Choose based on whether you want combined forecasting or a focused, independent engagement platform.


### What does the Salesloft and Clari merger mean for buyers?


The merger, closed December 3, 2025, pairs Salesloft's cadence with Clari's forecasting under one company, which is a real draw if you want both from one vendor. The trade-off is roadmap uncertainty common to large mergers: it is fair to ask which features get prioritized and how integrations evolve. Raise those questions directly in a sales conversation before committing to a multi-year term.


### Is Salesloft affected by the Drift breach?


Drift, a former sibling product, suffered a 2025 supply-chain breach reported by Google threat intelligence, and its retirement was announced in March 2026. Drift is a separate product from Salesloft's core sales engagement platform, so the breach is not a direct statement about the cadence tool. It is still reasonable to review the vendor's overall security posture and portfolio history as part of your evaluation.


### Which has better forecasting, Outreach or Salesloft?


Salesloft, because of the Clari merger. It offers native forecasting and revenue analytics tied to cadence activity from the same company. Outreach does not ship equivalent native forecasting; teams typically pair it with a separate tool. If forecasting integration is central to how you run the business, that is the clearest reason to choose Salesloft over Outreach.


### How much do Outreach and Salesloft cost?


Neither publishes public pricing. Outreach's reported figures are around $100 to $160 per user per month (an estimate), typically with implementation fees, sold through an enterprise process. Salesloft's numbers come through negotiation; third-party estimates put it around $125 to $165 per user per month, with the dialer usually an add-on, and you should factor in the forecasting side of the combined platform. Neither is a self-serve purchase, so expect a quote based on volume and term.


### Is there an alternative to both Outreach and Salesloft?


Yes. Both Outreach and Salesloft are human-driven engagement platforms: they organize and prompt what reps do next, but the reps still write, send, call, and reply. If you want the software to run more of the motion itself, Artisan's Ava is an[AI sales agent](https://www.artisan.co/ai-sales-agent) (AI BDR) that sources contacts, writes and sends outreach, and handles replies, priced on usage rather than per seat. Calling is built in: she dials the call steps and a rep handles the live conversation. It is a different category from a sequencer, suited to teams that want the motion owned end to end rather than orchestrated for reps.
